name: IHWF's Saturday Night Slaughter

date.source: No exact date survives on any of the three served hour-pages. The fed's own served news article, "The Insider," carries a CEO press-conference announcement of the fed's reopening "after two years" of dormancy following the held record's earlier, fully-dated 2001 run, bylined 8/2/2003; this broadcast's own opening segment stages that same reopening ("the return of the IHWF"), and its own dialogue elsewhere (Godfather: "it felt good to be back in the ring... on my road to winning the IHWF World Title once more") shows the World Title vacant/unheld by its own last-attested 2001 champion at the time of this broadcast, consistent with a later reopening rather than a continuation of the 2001 run. CORRECTION: the tier-1 pass dated this same broadcast to the 2001 run; a full reading of the fed's own reopening announcement in "The Insider" overturns that dating.

appearances.note: Accompanies Max Powers to the ring, then runs in against Jason Slade in the match's own closing angle.

notes: Hour Three of a three-hour reopening broadcast (see Hours One and Two, promotions/ihwf/archive/saturday-night-slaughter-1.html and -2.html) -- the fed's own served card page (saturday-night-slaughter-card.html) confirms the three-hour split and venue; TIER-1 CORRECTION (2026-09-01): the tier-1 pass framed this as "one of three surviving Saturday Night Slaughter broadcasts," reading Hours One-Three as three separate shows -- a full reading of all three hour-pages, and of the fed's own served card page, shows they are one broadcast split across three served documents. The Godfather defeats Chaos, then is ambushed after the match by Enforcer with a lead pipe; the Godfather's own post-match promo states he does not currently hold the World Title ("on my road to winning the IHWF World Title once more"), consistent with this broadcast dating after the held record's earlier, fully-dated 2001 title lineage rather than during it. Guest color commentator Atomic Mass, the fed's own CEO, sits in for this match and the main event. The main event, Jason Slade vs. Max Powers (with Mercenary accompanying Powers to the ring), ends with no official winner: after Slade sends Powers through a table, Mercenary runs in for a confrontation, and the show closes with the Godfather joining Mercenary -- named on-air "both members of Ultimate Justice" -- to jump Slade and put him through a second table.

notes: Hour One of a three-hour reopening broadcast (see Hours Two and Three, promotions/ihwf/archive/saturday-night-slaughter-2.html and -3.html) -- the fed's own served card page (saturday-night-slaughter-card.html) confirms the three-hour split and venue. William McCoy opens the card by attacking Mayhem backstage before their scheduled match, leaving no contest to record. Scotty Richards and Stevie Rich (billed by the fed's own announcers as "the man formerly known as Suicide") wrestle to no result after Mercenary runs in with a chair.

notes: Hour Two of a three-hour reopening broadcast (see Hours One and Three). Enforcer defeats Stevie Greene (billed "Stevie Green" on this page) with the finisher "Last Breat" [sic]. Mercenary defeats the Knight of Avalon, staged in full plate armor with a mace and a scimitar, in a weapons-heavy match won with a baseball bat; Logan Powers, Victor Durrant and Sinn Fein run in afterward, restrain Mercenary at swordpoint with his own discarded scimitar, and leave together -- "Logan and his crew," per the fed's own commentary, though no formal stable name is given for the trio.
